title: Number of Unique XOR Triplets I
summary: Given an integer array nums that is a permutation of numbers from 1 to n, calculate the total count of distinct XOR results for all possible triplets (i, j, k) where i <= j <= k.
statement: Given an integer array nums that is a permutation of numbers from 1 to n, calculate the total count of distinct XOR results for all possible triplets (i, j, k) where i <= j <= k.
constraints: nums is a permutation of integers 1 through n.
Choose indices i <= j <= k and compute nums[i] XOR nums[j] XOR nums[k].
Return the number of distinct results.
hints: Repeated indices allow every original value, while three distinct choices expand the reachable bit patterns for n>=3.
For n one or two, the answer is n; otherwise all values below the next power of two above n occur.
The permutation contains the low integers needed to construct every bit pattern in that range by three XOR choices.
editorial: The permutation contains the low integers needed to construct every bit pattern in that range by three XOR choices.

tests.explanation: The possible results are one and two, so the count is two.
For n=3 the attainable XOR values fill zero through three, giving four results.
